newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: IBEC calls for govt to restrain spending, cut tax.
newsitem.headline: IBEC calls for govt to restrain spending, cut tax.

text.p: The Irish Business and Employers Confederation (IBEC) made its preliminary pre-budget submission to the Irish government on Wednesday, calling for a reduction in public spending and lower taxes.
The efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the state-run sector must also be improved, IBEC said.

"Curbing the growth of public spending will provide greater resources for essential tax reform and tax reduction," IBEC said. "Tax reform will facilitate increases in the long term output and employment potential of the economy and will thus provide an overall benefit to the economy."

Tax reform would also enhance the competitiveness of the economy which was crucial to cope with Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) and the transition to an expected lower level of European Union structural funding, it said.
IBEC said a significant cut in the standard corporation tax rate would be self-financing through tax receipts from improved corporate profits.
Capital gains tax should be cut to 27 percent from 40 percent, and income tax should also be reduced along with PRSI (Pay-Related Social Insurance) payments, IBEC said.
"Lower employers' PRSI will help to maintain existing employment and generate new jobs. Lower income tax and employee PRSI will improve the prospects for wage moderation," it said.
Cutting tax on employment would also improve the incentive to work, crucial for tackling the problem of unemployment, IBEC added.
It said detailed work on its pre-budget submission would not be complete until later in the year, when a full submission would be made to the Finance and General Affairs Committee.
